issues.legal_issue: A watchman or caretaker who occupies property only on behalf of its owner does not acquire an independent right to the property through continued occupation and cannot resist the owner’s demand for possession on that basis.
material_facts: The property was owned by the society and had been dedicated for a community purpose.
The occupant’s father was employed by the society as a watchman and was permitted to live on the premises in that capacity.
After his father’s death, the occupant continued to serve as a watchman and remained in the premises with the society’s permission.
The occupant claimed adverse possession, but the Court found that the claim was not proved and that documents such as ration cards and house-tax receipts did not establish it.
issues.conclusion: The occupant had no independent right or interest in the property, including by adverse possession, and was not entitled to an injunction protecting his occupation against the owner. The appeals were dismissed and he was directed to vacate and hand over possession.
issues.legal_principle: A watchman, caretaker, servant or agent holding property for the principal acquires no right or interest in it merely through long occupation and must hand over possession when required. Courts should not protect such occupation against the lawful owner. The Court relied on Alagi Alamelu Achi v. Ponniah Mudaliar, AIR 1962 Madras 149, and the principles stated in Maria Margarida Sequeria Fernandes v. Erasmo Jack de Sequeria, (2012) 3 SCALE 550. It also noted that injunctions ordinarily depend on a prima facie case, balance of convenience and irreparable injury.

rule.if: civil_property_possession_dispute and owner_title_established and occupant_entered_as_watchman_or_caretaker and not independent_right_to_occupy_proved

predicates.civil_property_possession_dispute: The proceeding concerns a civil claim to possession of property.
predicates.owner_title_established: The person seeking possession has established legal title to the property.
predicates.occupant_entered_as_watchman_or_caretake: The occupant entered or remained on the property to look after it on behalf of its owner.
predicates.independent_right_to_occupy_proved: The occupant has proved a legal basis for occupation independent of the watchman or caretaker role.

issues.definition: When a civil property-possession dispute involves an owner with established title and an occupant who entered as a watchman or caretaker but has proved no independent right to occupy, the occupant has no right to retain the property against the owner.

issues.legal_issue: Once legal title to property is established, a person in occupation who claims a right to remain must specifically plead and prove the basis for that right.
material_facts: The society’s ownership of the property was established.
The occupant sought to remain in possession and relied on a claim of adverse possession and documents including ration cards and tax receipts.
The Court found that the adverse-possession claim lacked a factual basis and that the documents relied on did not establish it.
issues.conclusion: The occupant failed to establish a right to continue in possession, and the owner’s claim for possession prevailed.
issues.legal_principle: In a claim for recovery of possession, occupation by someone other than the legal title-holder is presumed to be under and subordinate to that title. The person resisting recovery must provide sufficiently detailed pleadings and supporting documents identifying the basis for remaining in possession, and must prove the pleaded facts. The Court relied on paragraphs 63–71 and 76 of Maria Margarida Sequeria Fernandes v. Erasmo Jack de Sequeria, (2012) 3 SCALE 550.

predicates.civil_property_possession_claim: The proceeding is a civil claim concerning recovery or protection of possession of property.
predicates.legal_title_established: A party has established legal title to the property in dispute.
predicates.another_person_claims_continuing_occupat: A person other than the title-holder occupies the property and claims a right to remain there.

issues.definition: In a civil property-possession claim, once legal title is established, an occupying person who claims to remain must plead and prove a right to do so.

issues.legal_issue: Courts in civil cases must critically examine pleadings and documents, focus the issues in dispute, and use available procedures to ascertain the truth.
material_facts: The occupant filed documents that the Court found irrelevant to the central dispute and capable of misleading the Court.
The Court found that he had suppressed material facts and advanced false or untenable pleas, including an unsupported adverse-possession claim.
The First Appellate Court was misled by the material and the dispute took many years to resolve.
The judgment discussed the need to scrutinize pleadings before granting injunctions or framing issues and to use discovery and examination procedures where appropriate.
issues.conclusion: The Court reiterated that judicial officers must examine pleadings and supporting documents with care, insist on sufficient particulars, and take appropriate steps to discover the truth and prevent misleading claims from distorting a civil case.
issues.legal_principle: Pleadings and documents are central to determining title and possession; vague or insufficient pleadings do not raise an issue, and a person claiming continued possession should state its factual basis with particularity and support it with documents. Order X Rule 2 of the Code of Civil Procedure permits oral examination of parties to clarify matters in controversy, and Section 30 CPC provides for discovery, inspection, production of documents, interrogatories and related measures. The Court relied on Maria Margarida Sequeria Fernandes v. Erasmo Jack de Sequeria, (2012) 3 SCALE 550; Dalip Singh v. State of U.P., (2010) 2 SCC 114; Mohanlal Shamji Soni v. Union of India, 1991 Supp (1) SCC 271; and Ritesh Tewari v. State of Uttar Pradesh, (2010) 10 SCC 677.

predicates.civil_case: The proceeding is a civil case.
predicates.pleadings_or_documents_are_material_to_t: The parties’ pleadings or documents bear on the facts or issues the court must decide.

issues.definition: In a civil case where pleadings or documents bear on the dispute, the court must scrutinize them and use available procedures to find the truth.

issues.legal_issue: A court should prevent a litigant from gaining an unfair advantage through false or irrelevant claims and should impose appropriate costs where litigation abuses the judicial process.
material_facts: The Court found that the occupant had suppressed material facts and introduced false, untenable and irrelevant pleas and documents.
The litigation over the premises continued for many years, and the Court considered that the occupant had obtained an undue benefit from the prolonged proceedings.
The Court stated that it would ordinarily have imposed heavy costs and ordered restitution, but imposed nominal costs in light of the occupant’s financial circumstances.
issues.conclusion: The Court dismissed the appeals, imposed nominal costs, and directed the occupant to vacate and hand over possession. It reiterated that costs and, where appropriate, restitution should be used to neutralize unfair benefits obtained through abuse of process.
issues.legal_principle: Courts should adopt a realistic approach to costs and restitution so that wrongful or undeserved advantages gained through litigation are neutralized and dishonest or frivolous litigation is discouraged. The Court relied on Ramrameshwari Devi v. Nirmala Devi, (2011) 8 SCC 249; Indian Council for Enviro-Legal Action v. Union of India, (2011) 8 SCC 161; Grindlays Bank Ltd. v. Income Tax Officer, (1980) 2 SCC 191; Kavita Trehan v. Balsara Hygiene Products, (1994) 5 SCC 380; South Eastern Coalfields Ltd. v. State of M.P., (2003) 8 SCC 648; and Marshall Sons & Co. (I) Ltd. v. Sahi Oretrans (P) Ltd., (1999) 2 SCC 325.

predicates.litigant_uses_false_or_irrelevant_claims: A litigant advances false, untenable or irrelevant claims or material.
predicates.conduct_causes_unfair_advantage_or_unnec: The litigant’s conduct produces an unfair benefit or unnecessarily prolongs the proceedings.

issues.definition: In civil litigation, when false or irrelevant claims produce an unfair advantage or unnecessary delay, the court should impose appropriate costs and neutralize that advantage.
